data.name: Aruba
data.summary: Aruba taxes residents on worldwide income (top rate 52%). Portfolio capital gains are exempt, but dividends and substantial-interest gains are taxed at a special 25% rate. There is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Interest on bank deposits is exempt. No wealthy-immigrant regime was verified.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation at progressive rates up to 52%. Dividends and gains on a substantial interest (25%+) are taxed at a special 25% rate; other capital gains are exempt. No inheritance or wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Facts and circumstances (centre of existence in Aruba). Non-Dutch nationals need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are exempt, except gains on a substantial interest (25%+ alone or with close relatives, at any time in the last 5 years), taxed at 25%.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Deemed sale of a substantial interest on emigration, or on death where heirs are non-residents, taxed at 25%. Shareholder loans above AWG 500,000 to a substantial shareholder are disguised dividends from 2025. Real estate transfer tax 3%/6% (buyer).

sources.title: BDO Aruba: Personal income tax (law effective 1 January 2026)

capital_gains.rate_basis: Deloitte Aruba 2026 and BDO (law effective 1 Jan 2026): special 25% rate on substantial-interest gains.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at the special 25% rate (BDO). A 10% dividend withholding applies to dividends paid to individuals. The temporary 10% reduced rate applied only to dividends distributed 2019-2023.
dividends.important_exceptions: Interest on deposits with supervised institutions in Aruba or abroad is exempt (BDO).

sources.title: BDO Aruba: Personal income tax (law effective 1 January 2026)

open_questions: Whether portfolio dividends (holding below 25%) fall under the 25% special rate or the progressive rates up to 52%; BDO describes 'dividends' generally under 25%.
dividends.rate_basis: BDO lists dividends among income taxed at the special 25% rate; Deloitte: foreign tax creditable up to the Aruban tax on that income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% on dividends (5% to companies within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; 0% under the IPC regime until 2027). No WHT on interest or royalties.
dividends.treaty_network: Tax Arrangement for the Kingdom of the Netherlands; very limited treaty network otherwise.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land tax for residents 0% to 0.6% by aggregate value bands; 0.6% for non-residents.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. Deloitte states inherited real property is not subject to transfer tax (though its transfer-tax paragraph also mentions acquisitions under succession).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Income tax: deemed disposal of a substantial interest at death if heirs are non-resident (25%).
open_questions: Deloitte's transfer-tax text is internally inconsistent on inheritances of real estate.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; donations of Aruban real estate may attract transfer tax (3%/6%).

residency.tax_residency_test: Centre of existence in Aruba (facts and circumstances).

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: Dutch nationals have privileged admission; others need a permit. Not researched.

corporate.summary: CIT 22%; participation exemption; IPC regime (10% profit tax, 0% WHT) abolished for financial years starting from 1 Jan 2026 (BDO).

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the five 4- and 5-bedroom houses on RE/MAX Aruba's residential rental page on 15 Oct 2026 (mostly recently rented): Ponton 24-a, Eagle Beach, 5 bed, USD 3,600; Wayaca 275, 4 bed, USD 3,596; Constantijn Huygenstraat villa, Oranjestad, 4 bed, USD 3,500; Monte Verde, 4 bed, USD 2,416; Tamarijn, 4 bed, USD 2,360. CENTURY 21 Aruba listed a 4-bedroom Westpunt home at USD 4,000 the same day. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: International School of Aruba (US-curriculum, the island's only English-language international school), Secondary School Grades 9-12 annual tuition, as shown on the school's admissions page in the Wayback Machine snapshot of 12 Jan 2026 (school year 2025-26; the page states no year): AWG 39,755 (USD 22,460); Grades 7-8 AWG 34,324. Plus a Capital Levy Fee of AWG 14,000 (USD 7,910) a year for new students and a AWG 375 application fee; 5% surcharge for monthly payment. ISA announced in March 2026 it would close after 2025-26; Quality Schools International took over management from 1 July 2026 and as QSI International School of Aruba publishes no 2026-27 tuition, only a USD 600 registration fee.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets; the app adds the federal layer. Local tax can generally be credited against US tax on the same foreign-source income only where the US foreign tax credit rules allow.

Portfolio dividend rate (25% vs progressive) to confirm.

succession.name: Aruba
succession.summary: Aruba has no forced heirship since its new inheritance law took effect on 1 September 2021, so a will can leave the estate to anyone. Children can still claim a capped lump sum, and a surviving spouse has statutory rights. Aruba has no trust law and the Hague Trusts Convention is not extended to it; a private foundation is not available in the full form found in Curaçao.
succession.family_claims: Book 4 gives a child a lump-sum claim against the heirs for care and upbringing (to age 18), living and study costs (to 21, extendable to 25) and unpaid work in the parent's household or business. The lump sum cannot exceed half the estate. The surviving spouse has statutory rights (legal division, usufruct of the home).
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states Aruba's conflict rule for the estate of a foreign national, or whether a foreigner may choose the law of their nationality.
succession.trust_note: The HCCH table shows the Netherlands' extension covering Curaçao only; Aruba is not listed, so the Convention is not in force there. No Aruban trust statute was found. Foundations (stichting) sit in Book 2 of the Civil Code, in force 1 January 2021; a 2019 commentary says a private foundation was considered and dismissed, so only ordinary foundations exist.
open_questions: Aruba's private international law rule for succession of foreign nationals was not sourced.
Transition rules for estates opened before 1 September 2021 were not read.
The text of Aruba's Book 4 was not read; the rules above come from a law-firm summary.
Whether Aruba has any trust statute or a private foundation form was not confirmed against Book 2 itself.
